regressions.issue: The array-bounds check against the same length as the loop bound is printed again in each iteration (Panic(50) lines +3), because the body's writes through the free pointer are no longer proved to miss the array header.
regressions.rule: The free pointer is at least the end of the last allocation (a symbolic floor, not only a constant one): writes at mem[64] + k then cannot alias an earlier array's header, and i >= len inside 'while i < len' (len unchanged) is dominated.

regressions.old: return memory from mem[64] len 96 * mem[32 * stor758A.length + 160] + 64; _37 = sha3(...) / stor[_37].field_8
regressions.issue: After the allocating loop, mem[64] has no known floor, so the encoding loop's writes may alias it: the return length keeps _25 - mem[64] (zero), and two mapping keys at mem[0] are printed as concat(mem[0]) (P4, 2 lines; the mapping is now named, though).
regressions.rule: A free pointer that starts above a constant floor and only grows keeps the floor through loops, so writes at mem[64] + k (k >= 0) miss [0, 96): cancel _25 - mem[64] and resolve keys written at mem[0].

new_findings.issue: The copy loop is now folded, but the call's 4-byte input is printed in the function-name position as a memory slice although it was just written as the decimals() selector.
new_findings.rule: Never print a memory slice as a function name; when the call input's bytes are known (written just before), name the function from its selector.

improvements: P6 fixed. 23 element-copy loops resolved (151 -> 128 while): encoded call data now folded, so transferFrom and the library delegatecall are decoded and SafeERC20/custom-error reverts decoded; two events print their arguments instead of raw memory. Struct-array init loop in getTransceiverInfo no longer rotated (P3), and its encode loop bounds on stor758A.length.
notes: Diff 1938 lines, reviewed function by function (10 changed). All 8 exponentiation loops of the transfer paths and the source loops are still present; the removed whiles are copies of encoded bytes. The low-level decimals() call drops a dead free-pointer update; the text stays consistent since nothing later depends on it.
summary: Low regressions only: dominated in-loop bounds checks printed again and an uncancelled _25 - mem[64] in getTransceiverInfo's return, both from a weaker free-pointer floor. Gains: copy loops folded, calls, reverts and events decoded; the decimals() call now shows its selector as a memory slice in the name.
